title: Reserved GPU credit hedging & SLA continuity prototype
creator: Asha Verma
description:
Goal: Design and validate a packaging prototype that (1) smooths customer spend volatility via a credit hedging model for reserved GPU commitments, (2) guarantees SLA continuity during transient capacity shortfalls using tiered fallback contracts, and (3) captures legal/security questionnaire (SQ) requirements into a contract template and operational runbook. This ticket covers product requirements, experiment plan, pricing simulations, and coordination with Legal, SalesOps, and Eng for a small pilot (10 customers).

Context: Many customers want reserved GPU capacity but are deterred by bill volatility during usage spikes and regional preemption. Sales has requested a commercial structure that (a) amortizes burst risk across a commitment window and (b) provides clear continuity guarantees when primary reserved pools are throttled. Legal needs a standard clause set for continuity and data segregation to speed SQ responses.

Scope: Prototype a "Hedge+Continuity" offer: a monthly reserved commitment with an adaptive credit buffer (hedge) that recharges based on trailing 30-day usage; an SLA continuity ladder with deterministic fallback options (model variants + regional failover + time-limited grace credits); and a contract appendix that maps these behaviors to SQ answers and audit artifacts. This does NOT include full Dedicated pricing catalogization for all SKUs — that is follow-on work.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment spec and pricing model documented and reviewed by Finance and SalesOps
Legal-approved contract appendix draft that answers top 10 SQ items for Dedicated capacity continuity
Two simulated customer billing traces (low-variance and high-spike) run through the hedging model with clear P50/P95 cost outcomes
Pilot rollout checklist and Eng runbook for automated fallback behaviors (regional failover, model variant fallback, credit deduction)
Stakeholder sign-off (PM, Sales, Legal, Eng) to proceed to pilot with 10 customers
milestones: 2025-02-18: Finalize hedging formula and simulation harness (owner: PM)
2025-02-25: Legal draft of contract appendix and SQ mapping (owner: Legal)
2025-03-04: Eng design review for fallback orchestration and billing hooks (owner: Eng)
2025-03-15: Run pricing sims and prepare pilot offer sheet (owner: Finance/SalesOps)
risks: Under-priced hedge could increase Redwood unit economics exposure if many pilots show correlated spikes
Fallback automation adds complexity to runtime routing and may create transient latencies impacting SLA perception
Legal may require additional audit controls for continuity guarantees that increase implementation time
Sales may over-index pilots on low-risk customers, biasing outcome signals
notes: Hedging model sketch: maintain a credit buffer sized to X% of committed capacity; credits replenish at a rate proportional to unused reservation each window; over-usage draws on credits, then on on-demand pricing once credits exhausted.

Continuity ladder: primary reserved pool (SLA 99.9) -> regional reserved failover (SLA 99.7, opt-in) -> short-term burst credits (grace, e.g., 72 hours) -> best-effort on-demand fallback with reduced throughput guarantee.
We will instrument per-customer telemetry to show how credits are consumed and surfaced in Console (cost & latency views) before pilot signings.
This ticket intentionally prototypes a limited contract appendix (3 pages) rather than a full MSA change — faster for pilots and SQ responses.
